title: ECHO-ADL: An image-based questionnaire for assessing hearing-specific activities of daily living (ADL) in people with hearing loss
summary:
Background:
Hearing loss can affect many areas of everyday life. However, only limited options are currently available to comprehensively and specifically assess difficulties in everyday life for people with hearing loss. The ECHO-ADL questionnaire, developed as part of this study, is intended to help systematically assess hearing-related difficulties in everyday life and thereby enable a better long-term assessment of the impact of hearing loss on everyday life.

Research question:
The aim of the study is to evaluate the newly developed ECHO-ADL questionnaire. In particular, the study will examine whether the questionnaire reliably and accurately captures hearing-related difficulties in everyday life. In addition, the study will investigate how the difficulties assessed by the questionnaire are related to general everyday functioning, quality of life, perceived hearing ability, and mood.

Methods:
The study aims to include people with different degrees of hearing loss (ranging from mild to severe or profound hearing loss / deafness), different types of hearing rehabilitation (e.g., hearing aids or cochlear implants), and different causes of hearing loss (e.g., age-related or illness-related). People without hearing loss will also participate as a comparison group. Participants will provide information about themselves and complete questionnaires assessing hearing-related difficulties in everyday life, general everyday functioning, quality of life and mood. In addition, tests will be conducted to assess cognitive functioning (e.g., memory tasks). The data will be statistically analyzed to determine whether the ECHO-ADL questionnaire is reliable, whether it measures the intended construct, and whether it can distinguish between people with and without hearing loss. A subgroup of participants with hearing loss will be asked to complete the ECHO-ADL questionnaire again after approximately six months. This will allow the reliability and stability of the questionnaire results over a longer period of time to be assessed.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
inclusion criteria (control group): individuals 18 years old or older, no audiologically confirmed hearing loss / no relevant self-reported hearing loss, no neurological or psychiatric disorders associated with clinically relevant cognitive or affective impairments; informed consent; sufficient language and visual abilities.

inclusion criteria (group of people with hearing loss): individuals 18 years old or older,
presence of an audiologically confirmed hearing loss; no neurological or psychiatric disorders associated with clinically relevant cognitive or affective impairments; informed consent, sufficient language and visual abilities.
Exclusion criteria:
exclusion criteria (control group): individuals younger than 18 years, confirmed hearing loss / relevant self-reported hearing loss, neurological or psychiatric disorders associated with clinically relevant cognitive or affective impairments; no informed consent; non sufficient language and visual abilities.

exclusion criteria (group of people with hearing loss): individuals younger than 18 years,
absence of an audiologically confirmed hearing loss; neurological or psychiatric disorders associated with clinically relevant cognitive or affective impairments; no informed consent, non sufficient language and visual abilities.
